userestrict.head: Conditions Governing Use
userestrict.p: Ford Foundation has title, copyright and literary rights in the collection, in so far as it holds them.

The Rockefeller Archive Center has authority to grant permission to cite and publish material from the collection. Permission to publish extensive excerpts, or material in its entirety, will be referred to the Ford Foundation.

acqinfo.head: Immediate Source of Acquisition
acqinfo.p: Ford Foundation archive was deposited at the RAC in 2011. Ford Foundation records, correspondence, reports, program files, and officers' papers were transferred to and accessioned by the RAC beginning in 2011. Accessions continue as necessary.
This material was transferred to the RAC as part of three larger accessions between 2021 and 2023. These accessions were ingested by the RAC as Accessions 2021:020, 2021:134, and 2023:069.

bioghist.head: Biographical / Historical
bioghist.p: The Ford Foundation opened its office in Jakarta, Indonesia in 1953. As part of the Foundation's international programming, it fell under its South and Southeast Asia and later Asia and Pacific umbrellas alongside the Foundation's offices in India, Pakistan, Myanmar (Burma), Malaysia, Philippines, Thailand, Bangladesh, and Japan at various points.

Following a program reorganization at the Foundation, the Jakarta Office became the Southeast Asia Office and managed programming for Indonesia and the broader Southeast Asia region. Offices in Bangkok, Thailand and Manila, Philippines operated under it. In the mid-1990s, the Foundation's Southeast programming split between Indonesia and the Philippines and a separate Thailand and Vietnam program. The Indonesia program later broke from the Philippines program, and the Jakarta Office has concentrated on programming for Indonesia into the present.
The Jakarta Office closed for more than a year between 1965 and 1967 due to the political climate in Indonesia.

Throughout the years, the Jakarta Office's programming has focused on education, agriculture, social forestry, natural resources, economic development, public administration, health, human rights, family planning and population, and arts and culture.

Ford Foundation Representatives for Indonesia have included: Michael Harris, Frank Miller, John Bresnan, Guillaume de Spoelberch, Theordore Smith, Tom Kessinger, David Winder, Mary Zurbuchen, Suzanne Siskel, and Meiwita Budiharsana.

arrangement.p: The collection is comprised of one series. Original order was maintained as much as possible.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The collection contains the files of the Ford Foundation's field office in Jakarta, Indonesia. It consists of one series of subject files.

The programming responsibility and organization of the Jakarta Office has shifted over its decades of operation since opening in 1953, and the specific holdings of this collection reflect those changes. The files primarily originate from between the 1950s and the late 1980s. If additional records are added to the collection, they may document more recent history of the Jakarta Office.

In the earlier files in the collection, the Jakarta Office operated under the International Division's programs for South and Southeast Asia and then Asia and the Pacific. These files show the Jakarta Office's grant support for teacher training and education, English language training, public administration training and development, technical and vocational education, agriculture, law, and rural community development in Indonesia. The Indonesia Teacher Training Colleges (PTPG/FKIP/IKIP) project between the Foundation and the State University of New York (SUNY) Program is especially highlighted.

A later group of files in the collection from the 1980s originate from when the Jakarta Office served as the Foundation's Southeast Asia Office and managed the Foundation's programming for the broader Southeast Asia region in addition to Indonesia. They concern economic development and refugees in Southeast Asia and Foundation programming related to Vietnam.

Common material formats found within the collection include correspondence, memos, reports, grant related documents, meeting materials, invoices, press clippings, and articles. There are also several photographs in the collection.

did.unittitle: Subject files
did.physdesc: Many of the earlier created documents in the series from the 1950s have been impacted by rust from various metal fasteners originally used to keep the material together. The damage and residue have not damaged the text content of the documents, but the paper should be handled with care.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series contains subject files created and maintained by the Ford Foundation's field office in Jakarta, Indonesia. The subject files primarily document the Jakarta Office's program activities in Indonesia and other Southeast Asia countries between the 1950s and the late 1980s.

Files originating from the 1950s to early 1970s show the Jakarta Office's early emphasis on teacher training and education in Indonesia. The documents use various terms when referring to Indonesian Teacher Training Colleges including PTPG (Perguruan Tinggi Pendidikan Guru), FKIP (Fakultas Keguruan dan Ilmu Pendidikan), and IKIP (Institut Keguran dan Ilmu Pendidikan). A major component of this programming concerned the Teacher Training Colleges program between the Foundation and the State University of New York (SUNY).

Related and additional areas of program focus that appear in the earlier files include technical and vocational education, public administration and development, agriculture, law, and community development. Several of these files are organized around the consultants and training associates the Foundation contracted to assist these projects. Others are organized around the closing of the grants.

A different group of materials in the series was created at a later point in the Jakarta Office's history. They reflect the Jakarta Office's broader responsibility for the Southeast Asia region and concern economic development and refugees in the region as well as the Foundation's programming related to Vietnam in the years leading to normalized relations between Vietnam and the United States.
Significant grants documented within the series include:
The Republic of Indonesia (05600245) for the Indonesian English Language Teacher Training Program
The Republic of Indonesia (05600319) for advanced training for basic agricultural research
The Republic of Indonesia (05700001) for agricultural vocational training in Indonesia
The Republic of Indonesia (05700172) for support to Community Development Training Center in Indonesia
The Republic of Indonesia (05900479) for development of English Language Teaching Materials
The Republic of Indonesia (05800192) for scientific laboratory equipment and supplies for government universities
The Republic of Indonesia (06000099) for Faculties of education and teacher training (FKIP's)
The Research Foundation of State University of New York (SUNY) (06200019) for Graduate English language project and teacher training projects at Indonesian faculties of education
Indiana University (06300293) for the Institute for Clerical Training - PAP (Pendidikan Administrasi Perkantoran/Education for Office Administration)
Ford Foundation Foundation-Administered Project (FAP) (06490423) Program Specialist and Consultant Services for the Foundation's Program in South and Southeast Asia
Other grants with significant documentation are noted at the file level.
